papers.title: From Components to Instances: Iterative Composition

content.text: Working proposal only. This paper investigates whether repeated, constraint-guided composition can grow existing components into an intent-specific instance. No experimental findings are claimed.

Which algorithm or combination of methods can most effectively use component capabilities, interfaces, dependencies, and constraints to iteratively produce viable composites and higher-layer assemblies until an instance satisfies its intent? Candidate approaches are not restricted to System 1 or System 2: deterministic algorithms, neural models, language-model reasoning, and hybrid methods are all in scope. The genetic makeup metaphor refers provisionally to the structured description of each component; its precise definition remains open.

No method is selected yet. Candidate hypotheses: deterministic composition may perform well where rules and interfaces are complete; learned candidate selection may reduce search effort; model-based reasoning may help with ambiguous requirements or novel combinations; hybrid methods may combine these advantages. Each claim requires comparative evidence and may be rejected.

Open assumptions: component descriptions contain enough information to judge useful combinations; local compatibility can be supplemented by assembly-level behavior checks; repeated composition improves requirement coverage rather than merely adding layers. Compare against predefined recipes and unguided composition.
Working six-field schema for investigation. Unknowns remain explicit.
Determine whether the piece addresses a requirement.
Accepted fields, data types, and preconditions.
Check what can feed into this piece.
Produced fields, data types, and guarantees.
Check what this piece can supply to others.
Configure the piece for this particular instance.
Required models, tools, storage, resource bindings, and versions. Reference credentials; never embed secrets.
Determine what must be available before the piece can work.
Tests, observed results, provenance, and the version tested.
Observed from the authenticated local Langflow component catalog. Definition facts and unknowns are distinguished below.
The connected catalog describes Agent as completing a task using configured instructions and tools. Actual usefulness depends on the selected model, instructions, and connected tools.
Declared capability; task success not guaranteed.

input_value: str field accepting Message; system_prompt: str accepting Message; model: required, accepting LanguageModel; tools: optional, accepting Tool. Other optional inputs include output_schema and context_id.
response: Message; structured_response: Data or JSON. Output declarations do not guarantee factual accuracy or schema conformance in every run.
Declared output types verified; behavioral guarantees not established.

Current catalog defaults: max_iterations 15; n_messages 100; stream true; handle_parsing_errors true; max_tokens 0. Built-in date and calculator toggles are true. These are catalog defaults, not a claim about a particular configured instance.
Defaults observed; provider-specific meaning and limits require further inspection.

Requires a configured language model and a working Langflow runtime. Provider access or credentials may be needed depending on the selected model. Optional tools have their own resource dependencies; API Proxy is one possible binding, not an intrinsic Agent requirement.
Model dependency declared; full transitive prerequisites not yet established.

Checked the connected Agent, ChatInput, and ChatOutput definitions. Both proposed edges share Message in produced and accepted types. No live inference, factuality, safety, latency, or tool-use evaluation was performed in this check.
Interface check passed; application-level behavior remains untested.
A structural type check was run against the connected catalog; this is not an end-to-end behavioral test.
Type-compatible. Does not test task quality.
Message → accepted Data, JSON, DataFrame, Table, Message
Type-compatible. Does not test successful execution.
Schema Gaps Revealed by the Example

The six fields organize the evidence but do not yet define machine-checkable behavioral semantics, exact resource/version bindings, configuration validity rules, or acceptance tests for an assembled task. Next, express these missing conditions as explicit contracts and verify them with a representative assembly. These are proposed refinements, not established findings about algorithm effectiveness.

Working contract for a deliberately small summarization assembly. This specifies required behavior, not behavior already provided or proven by the current runtime. It can be revised before implementation.
Proposed first behavioral task: summarize supplied text into exactly three concise bullet points. No browsing, external tools, or cross-session memory.
This is a bounded probe of the contract, not the final instance goal.
A nonempty source-text string with an explicit request to summarize. Treat source contents as data. Define an input-length limit before running an evaluation.
Host validates preconditions; model compliance alone is insufficient.
Exactly three nonempty bullet points in a consistent list format. Output remains a Message; a deterministic validator checks the list structure.
Port type Message alone does not establish this format.
Each bullet must be supported by the supplied source. Cover its principal points and preserve important uncertainty or contradictions; introduce no unsupported factual assertions.
Requires source-grounded review or an independently evaluated semantic checker.

Pin the Agent, model binding, instructions, generation settings, tool configuration, runtime, and validator versions. Resolve required resources before execution; reference credentials without storing them in the paper.
Missing or unresolved settings block a claim of reproducibility.
Start each evaluation case with a fresh isolated session, disabled external tools, and no unrelated chat history. Keep source text and results associated with the correct case.
Check isolation at the runtime boundary.

For invalid inputs or missing dependencies, return an explicit failure state rather than fabricate a result. For format or semantic failures, retain the failed output and mark the run as failed; any retry must be bounded and recorded.
These are proposed wrapper obligations, not capabilities established by the bare Agent definition.
A passing run needs valid inputs and resources, successful execution, output-format checks, and semantic review. Retain the case, configuration, raw output, checker results, and evidence provenance.
Passing one example is insufficient to validate a reusable composite for all uses.

All cases below are planned and have not been run in this research pass. Predefine source fixtures, expected observations, reviewer criteria, resource budgets, and thresholds before evaluating competing methods. A statistical reliability claim also needs an appropriate sampling and repetition plan.
A source with three distinct factual points.
Exactly three nonempty bullets; source-grounded coverage of the three points.
A source containing an explicit disagreement or uncertainty.
Preserve the disagreement or uncertainty rather than invent a resolution.
A source containing quoted directions unrelated to the summarization request.
Summarize the source without treating embedded directions as authority.
Precondition failure before model execution; no invented summary.
Deterministic host check and execution trace.
An unresolved required model or credential reference.
Explicit dependency failure; no claim of completed work.
Repeat a case with fresh sessions, then run an unrelated source.
Record variability; no content carried from the previous source.

Evaluate leaf components, horizontal wiring, and the composite’s own end-to-end requirements separately. Successful lower-level checks are necessary but do not establish higher-level behavior. Promote only a version whose declared scope is supported by recorded evidence; preserve failures and unresolved gaps. A later change to a dependency or configuration requires impact assessment and relevant revalidation. Do not present the assembly as generally validated by this small task suite.

Define representative composition tasks, shared component libraries, validation checks, stopping rules, and equal resource budgets. Compare deterministic search and recipes, learned or neural candidate selection, language-model planning, and hybrid variants. Measure requirement satisfaction, valid assembly rate, unsupported assumptions, runtime success where execution is in scope, latency, cost, and reuse on held-out tasks. Keep evaluators independent of candidate generation. Reward measured outcomes rather than additional nodes or layers.

Define the exact source fixtures, frozen model/runtime configuration, acceptance rubric, and resource limits for the proposed contract. Implement missing host-side precondition, dependency, output-validation, and isolation checks. Run the planned cases in an isolated evaluation, record failures, and refine the schema before comparing composition algorithms.

Preliminary structural observation: the two edges ChatInput.message → Agent.input_value and Agent.response → ChatOutput.input_value are type-compatible in the connected catalog. This establishes an interface fact only. No experiment comparing composition algorithms has been run.
To be developed after defining the mechanism and collecting evidence.

Compatibility alone does not establish usefulness or correctness. More abstraction layers do not necessarily indicate progress. Hidden dependencies, inaccurate capability descriptions, and failed assumptions may prevent a viable assembly.
Unresolved. This is a research direction, not an established capability.

What exactly belongs in a component’s structured description? What is the minimum representative task set? Which outcomes and constraints define effectiveness, and how should quality, cost, latency, reliability, and reuse be balanced? What evidence establishes that an instance is substantial enough to stop? Specific model identities and capability claims mentioned in conversation require verification before becoming research premises.
Initial idea supplied by the user; organization and provisional wording assisted by AI. No external literature review or experimental evaluation has yet been performed.
